params.justification: SUP-002's rolling 14-day on-time delivery rate has fallen to 40.5% (79 deliveries), a -50.3pp deviation below the 90-day baseline of 90.8% (321 deliveries). This exceeds the RB-001 §1 detection threshold of 20pp and is corroborated by a robust z-score of -3.63 (median/MAD method per RB-001 §2), confirming the supplier is a statistical outlier within the population. A performance review case is required per RB-001 §3. Pending confirmation that the drop is not attributable to a single bulk order or site closure.

outcome.root_cause: SUP-002 has experienced a severe and statistically confirmed degradation in on-time delivery performance. Over the most recent 14-day rolling window (79 deliveries — well above the 20-delivery minimum sample floor), the supplier's on-time rate has fallen to 40.5%, compared to a 90-day baseline of 90.8% across 321 deliveries. This represents a -50.3 percentage-point deviation, more than double the 20pp threshold required to treat the exception as a genuine performance shift rather than noise. The deviation is further corroborated by a robust z-score of -3.63, calculated using median and median absolute deviation across the supplier population (as required by RB-001 §2), confirming SUP-002 is an outlier relative to the broader supplier base and not merely reflecting a market-wide disruption. Per RB-001 §3, a supplier performance review case must be opened and the category buyer notified. Re-sourcing is not warranted on a single fortnight of data, and expediting is not justified without evidence of SKU cover falling below ten days (RB-001 §5).

params.justification: SKU-1003 has 41,000 units on hand against a safety stock of 90,000 (deficit: -49,000 units) and only 5.0 days of cover, breaching both the safety stock and 14-day cover thresholds defined in RB-002 §1. In-transit quantity is 0, so no duplicate suppression applies (RB-002 §3). Cover is below 7 days, meeting the expedite consideration threshold in RB-002 §2 — the human approver should assess expedited freight at time of release. Quantity stated is the minimum to restore safety stock; planning should confirm final order quantity and lead time.

outcome.root_cause: SKU-1003 meets both stockout risk criteria under RB-002: on-hand inventory (41,000 units) is 49,000 units below the safety stock level (90,000 units), and days of cover (5.0) is below the 14-day threshold. With zero units in transit, there is no in-flight replenishment to suppress a new request. Cover is also below the 7-day expedite threshold, but per RB-002 §5 and RB-004 §1, a replenishment request commits spend and requires human release — automation may only prepare and recommend it.

params.justification: SUP-005 on-time delivery rate has fallen to 62.0% over the last 14 days (44 deliveries), 29.0pp below the 91.0% baseline (356 deliveries), exceeding the RB-001 §1 threshold of -20pp. Deviation is corroborated by a robust z-score of -2.10 (median/MAD method, per RB-001 §2). Sample size of 44 meets the minimum floor of 20. Supplier is strategic-tier; commercial owner escalation is required before any contractual action per RB-001 §4. Human review should confirm no single bulk order or site closure explains the drop before further action.

outcome.root_cause: SUP-005 has experienced a statistically significant and operationally material degradation in on-time delivery performance over the most recent 14-day rolling window. The observed OTD rate of 62.0% across 44 deliveries is 29.0 percentage points below the 91.0% baseline established over 356 deliveries, exceeding the RB-001 detection threshold of 20 percentage points. The deviation is corroborated by a robust z-score of -2.10, calculated using median and MAD across the supplier population as required by RB-001 §2, confirming SUP-005 is an outlier rather than a reflection of a market-wide move. The recent sample of 44 deliveries comfortably exceeds the minimum floor of 20 deliveries specified in RB-001 §1, making the rate reliable. As a strategic-tier supplier, RB-001 §4 requires escalation to the commercial owner before any contractual action; the appropriate automated response is therefore to open a supplier performance review case and notify the category buyer, pending that escalation. Re-sourcing is explicitly prohibited on a single fortnight of data per RB-001 §3.

params.justification: SKU-1002 on-hand is 48,600 units, which is 11,400 units below the safety stock level of 60,000 units. Days-of-cover is 9.0 days, below the 14-day threshold. Both RB-002 §1 conditions are met. In-transit quantity of 90,000 units arriving in 3 days was checked per RB-002 §3 and will restore cover once landed; however, the current position is below safety stock and the in-transit has not yet arrived. Cover is 9.0 days (above the 7-day expedite trigger), so standard replenishment at standard lead time is the proportionate response. Human release required per RB-002 §5.

outcome.root_cause: SKU-1002 meets both RB-002 stockout risk criteria: on-hand inventory (48,600 units) is below the safety stock threshold (60,000 units) by 11,400 units, and days-of-cover stands at 9.0 days — under the 14-day minimum. The in-transit quantity of 90,000 units arriving in 3 days is sufficient to restore cover well above safety stock once it lands, but cover has not yet been restored at the time of this exception. Because cover is between 7 and 14 days (9.0 days), standard replenishment is the appropriate response per RB-002 §2; expedited freight is only warranted below 7 days of cover. Per RB-002 §5, a replenishment request commits spend and a delivery slot, so a human must release it — automation may only prepare and recommend.
